navratri 2026 rashifal — all 12 rashis, the short version

read these by your moon sign. i'm serious about this now. quick festival-week reads:

mesh (aries). the moon sits in your partnership house on day 1 with retrograde venus right next to it. old conversations reopen — a stalled talk with a partner or a client comes back around. don't rush to close it, venus retrograde rewards the second draft. family festival duties pile up mid-week, agree early and keep travel plans flexible.

vrishabh (taurus). work and routine get the spotlight as navratri begins. trim one draining habit this week, your energy will thank you by dussehra. money-wise, venus retrograde says review subscriptions and shared expenses instead of starting new ones.

mithun (gemini). creativity and romance run high in the first half. if you've been sitting on an idea, day 3-4 is good for giving it shape — but keep contracts loose, mercury retrograde starts october 24 and anything signed now should have wiggle room.

kark (cancer). mars in your sign makes emotions run hot all nine days. when family tempers flare over festival planning, be the calm one — it pays off disproportionately this week. health: watch acidity and sleep, the usual navratri fasting traps.

simha (leo). confidence is up but so is the urge to control every family decision. don't. delegate one thing and watch the week go smoother. career-wise, something you pitched weeks ago resurfaces around day 6-7.

kanya (virgo). the sun is in your sign till october 17, then moves to libra. practical planning is your superpower right now — budgets, lists, festival logistics. just don't let perfectionism turn navratri prep into a second job.

tula (libra). your season starts in every sense — moon enters your sign on day 1, sun follows on the 17th, and it's your venus going retrograde. relationships are THE theme of your navratri. review, don't react. an old connection reaching out mid-week deserves a real conversation, not a reaction.

vrishchik (scorpio). introspective nine days. sleep and rest matter more than usual — broken rest is the classic complaint this week. something financial that's been stuck starts moving after dussehra. till then, document everything in writing.

dhanu (sagittarius). friendships and long-range goals light up. a group plan — garba night, a trip, a shared project — comes together nicely around day 5-6. watch sharp words at family meals though, they land harder than you mean them to.

makar (capricorn). career visibility is high. the work you do during navratri gets noticed, especially around day 7 when the sun shifts. just don't sacrifice every evening to the office — the festival is the point, and burnout helps nobody.

kumbh (aquarius). learning and perspective expand this week. good nine days for starting a course, reading something dense, or finally understanding a family elder's point of view. money: avoid lending during venus retrograde, even to people you like.

meen (pisces). emotional depth is the theme — prayer, reflection, and honest conversations land well. shared finances need a clear-eyed look before dussehra. trust your intuition this week, but pair it with one practical check before any big call.

and remember — dussehra on october 20 is the traditional green light for new beginnings. if you've been waiting to launch something, that date is circled for a reason.

one more thing worth knowing: navratri isn't the only thing moving this month. mercury goes retrograde on october 24, right after dussehra, which is why the old advice says get contracts, travel bookings and big purchases sorted before then. and jupiter enters leo on october 31, opening a genuinely good stretch for learning and creative work. the festival is the warm-up — the last week of october is where the bigger shifts land.

fasting without the drama

navratri fasting rules get overcomplicated every year, so here's the sane version. most people do one meal a day or fruit-and-milk fasts, skipping grains, non-veg, alcohol, onion and garlic. the mistakes people actually make: going zero-water (don't, that's not required in most traditions), breaking the fast with a massive fried feast on day 10 (your stomach will file a complaint), and treating the fast as a weight-loss hack instead of a discipline practice.

if you have a health condition, are pregnant, or take daily medication — talk to your doctor, not your aunt's whatsapp group. the goddess will understand.
